heading: Seven things Helix does that raw agents don't.
description: Helix is the orchestrator sitting on top of your favourite AI coding agent. It turns every prompt into small, reviewable, repo-aware changes — and gives every kind of user the workflow they actually want.

items.title: Atomic decomposition
items.description: Every prompt is broken into atomic cards with explicit inputs, outputs, and acceptance criteria — so no change is bigger than a human can review.

items.title: Parallel agent orchestration
items.description: Helix fans out work to multiple agents, runs independent atoms in parallel, and gates downstream steps on the ones they depend on. No more serial waiting.

items.title: Repo-aware verification
items.description: Each atom is checked against the rest of your repo — types, tests, lint, and your own quality scripts — before any PR is opened.

items.title: Reviewable PR output
items.description: Helix ships one small PR per atom, with a clear description, the prompt that produced it, and the verification log. Reviewing AI code finally feels normal.

items.title: Persona-targeted workflows
items.description: Solo founder, staff engineer, EM, tech lead, or AI engineer — Helix surfaces the right defaults, dashboards, and guardrails for each role.

items.title: Multi-stack support
items.description: TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, Ruby, Java — Helix reads your repo, picks the right toolchain per file, and verifies with the project's own scripts.

items.title: Quality bar enforcement
items.description: Define your quality bar once — coverage thresholds, lint rules, review checklist — and Helix blocks any PR that doesn't meet it.
